formulas.name: tm_shell_n0_is_dual_polynomial_value
formulas.expression: C cumulative = 2 + sum_{k=1..n}(10k^2+2); single = 1 + sum_{k=1..n}(10k^2+2); dual = sum_{k=0..n}(10k^2+6k+2)

formulas.notes: NO_CODE; reading of tm_shell_cumulative_population in the centre model: the C code evaluates 10k^2+2 uniformly from k = 0, so its n = 0 term 2 is the polynomial value, which is the dual-centre count at n = 0 (2 points), while its shells for n >= 1 are single-centre shells (10n^2+2) and not dual-centre shells (10n^2+6n+2); the function therefore mixes a dual-centre centre with single-centre shells; consistent single-centre cumulative is 1, 13, 55, 147 and consistent dual-centre cumulative is 2, 20, 74, 184; the C values 2, 14, 56, 148 match neither; no code changed, owner decision which centre model is intended

formulas.name: fcc_shell_single_vs_dual
formulas.expression: single: 10n^2 + 2 for n >= 1; dual: 10n^2 + 6n + 2 for n >= 0
formulas.specification: single: 10n^2 + 2 for n >= 1; dual: 10n^2 + 6n + 2 for n >= 0
formulas.notes: NO_CODE; FCC (cuboctahedral) lattice shells at graph distance n: single centre 10n^2 + 2 for n >= 1 (1 at n = 0, so the polynomial gives 2 there), dual centre (two adjacent points) 10n^2 + 6n + 2 for every n >= 0; the dual shell exceeds the single shell by 6n for n >= 1; no alternation in n (first differences of the dual shell 16, 36, 56, 76, constant second difference 20); exact breadth-first counts to n = 10 in the script

formulas.name: zd_single_centre_shell_n0_oscillation
formulas.notes: NO_CODE; the L1 shell polynomial P_d(n) of Z^d (number of points at distance n from one point, polynomial for n >= 1) takes the value 1 - (-1)^d at n = 0, which alternates 2, 0, 2, 0 with the parity of the dimension, while the true count at n = 0 is 1, so the true count minus P_d(0) is (-1)^d; derivation: the generating function ((1+x)/(1-x))^d has equal numerator and denominator degree, so the coefficient sequence is P_d(n) for n >= 1 and P_d(0) + (-1)^d at n = 0 (the polynomial part of the division is the limit at infinity, (-1)^d); recomputed exactly for d = 1..8 by the script; the oscillation is in the dimension, no alternation in n was found
